chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), like it.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), the source of the narration
key_terms.الْمُفَضَّل: Al-Mufaddal, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.زَيْدٌ الشَّحَّام: Zayd al-Shahham, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.عَمْرُو بْنُ عُثْمَان: Amr ibn Uthman, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Like it / the same, indicating the text is identical to a previous hadith

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one heir acknowledges a debt for the deceased?
ai.summary: This concise narration from al-Istibsar confirms the validity of a single heir acknowledging a debt on behalf of the deceased, reinforcing the principle that such admission binds the estate without requiring proof from other heirs. By citing 'like it' (mithlahu), Shaykh al-Tusi links this ruling to the broader jurisprudential consensus on inheritance liabilities, emphasizing the reliability of the chain through prominent figures like al-Mufaddal and Zayd al-Shahham.
